Runtime reference

shdr 1.0.0 API reference

A C++11 header for CPU and GPU compute pipelines. The build helper turns native GLSL into CPU adapters and embeds GPU source. Applications create kernels, bind resources and run dispatches. Read or download the single-file runtime header.

Start with the walkthrough. Read about resources and bindings, supported shader features, asynchronous execution, imaging, event-camera processing, neural models, signal processing and public data. The example catalog connects each complete program to its kernels.

BackendMinimum requirement
CPUC++11 compiler and host resources.
OpenGL ESES 3.1 with GLSL ES 3.10, or ES 3.2 with GLSL ES 3.20.
Desktop OpenGLGL 4.3 with GLSL 4.30, or a newer supported profile.

Enable SHDR_ENABLE_EGL=1 and link EGL to create a headless GPU device. An existing application context can supply its own function resolver. GPU calls and final resource release use the context thread. The runtime handles transfers, dispatches, fence polling and bounded CPU work queues.

Resources and synchronization

template <class T, std::size_t N> class array

A fixed-size array for GLSL local variables and function arguments.
The size must be positive. Default construction initializes every element to
its zero/default value. component construction requires exactly N elements.
Copy construction and assignment copy all elements. Use length() to query
the element count and operator[] to select an element with a valid index.
Resource ports define buffer and uniform memory layouts separately.

template <class T> class buffer

Shared typed std430 storage, owned or borrowed, with automatic CPU/GPU synchronization.

class pipeline

An ordered pipeline, composed with >> or +=. Resources link stages by shared storage.
GPU stages issue memory barriers. CPU/GPU transitions transfer authoritative resource contents.
Running again observes updated uniforms and resource bindings. CPU execution
completes each stage before returning. GPU execution queues stages in order.
Request host data or use an explicit wait to observe GPU completion.

class submission

A movable handle for one queued GPU pipeline.
ready() performs a zero-timeout fence query. wait(timeout) bounds the requested
driver wait. wait() explicitly waits for completion. Destroying a handle
schedules pending fence and resource cleanup on the device context thread.
Device garbage collection releases those retained resources after completion.

shdr.h, line 3615 
class executor

A bounded CPU executor for independent pipeline jobs.
Each submit() snapshots kernels, uniforms and resource bindings. Snapshots
have independent invocation state, while buffers and images retain shared
storage. Give concurrent jobs distinct writable resources, such as ring slots.
Queue saturation throws immediately. Futures report results or exceptions.
Destroying a future releases its result handle, while the executor retains
the job until completion. shutdown() drains accepted jobs and joins workers.
Executor destruction also drains and joins them.

A vector with two, three or four components of one scalar type.

scalar, vector and matrix arguments from left to right. matrices contribute

213    } // Finish the length operation.

225    array(std::initializer_list<T> values) : elements_() { // Initialize fixed-array storage from the supplied values.
226        if (values.size() != N) // Reject a brace list with the wrong element count.
227            throw std::invalid_argument("array initializer element count mismatch"); // Report an initializer length mismatch.

876/** @brief Determinant using partial-pivot elimination. */
877template <class T, std::size_t N> T determinant(mat<T, N, N> a) { // Accept the matching input types and dimensions.
878    T result(1); // Begin the determinant product with multiplicative identity.
879    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < N; ++i) { // Visit each component needed by this calculation.
880        std::size_t pivot = i; // Begin with the current row as the pivot candidate.
881        for (std::size_t r = i + 1; r < N; ++r) // Visit each matrix row.
882            if (std::abs(a[i][r]) > std::abs(a[i][pivot])) // Prefer the row with the larger pivot magnitude.
883                pivot = r; // Use the stronger row for the next pivot.
884        if (a[i][pivot] == T(0)) // Detect a singular column before division.
885            return T(0); // Compute the determinant with row pivoting.
886        if (pivot != i) { // Swap rows when a better pivot was found.
887            for (std::size_t c = 0; c < N; ++c) { // Visit each matrix column.
888                T temp = a[c][i]; // Save an entry while exchanging the two rows.
889                a[c][i] = a[c][pivot]; // Update this matrix entry during row elimination or exchange.
890                a[c][pivot] = temp; // Update this matrix entry during row elimination or exchange.
891            } // Finish this component or matrix pass.
892            result = -result; // Reverse the determinant sign after a row exchange.
893        } // Finish handling this condition.
894        T diagonal = a[i][i]; // Save the pivot value before normalizing the row.
895        result *= diagonal; // Multiply the determinant by the next diagonal value.
896        for (std::size_t r = i + 1; r < N; ++r) { // Visit each matrix row.
897            T factor = a[i][r] / diagonal; // Find the amount of the pivot row to eliminate.
898            for (std::size_t c = i + 1; c < N; ++c) // Visit each matrix column.
899                a[c][r] -= factor * a[c][i]; // Update this matrix entry during row elimination or exchange.
900        } // Finish this component or matrix pass.
901    } // Finish this component or matrix pass.
902    return result; // Return the completed result.
903} // Finish the determinant operation.
904/** @brief Inverse using partial-pivot Gauss-Jordan elimination.

906 */
907template <class T, std::size_t N> mat<T, N, N> inverse(mat<T, N, N> a) { // Accept the matching input types and dimensions.
908    mat<T, N, N> out(T(1)); // Keep an independent value for the result or aliased inputs.
909    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < N; ++i) { // Visit each component needed by this calculation.
910        std::size_t pivot = i; // Begin with the current row as the pivot candidate.
911        for (std::size_t r = i + 1; r < N; ++r) // Visit each matrix row.
912            if (std::abs(a[i][r]) > std::abs(a[i][pivot])) // Prefer the row with the larger pivot magnitude.
913                pivot = r; // Use the stronger row for the next pivot.
914        if (a[i][pivot] == T(0)) { // Detect a singular column before division.
915            for (std::size_t c = 0; c < N; ++c) // Visit each matrix column.
916                out[c] = vec<T, N>(std::numeric_limits<T>::quiet_NaN()); // Store the computed component in the independent result.
917            return out; // Return the completed result.
918        } // Finish handling this condition.
919        if (pivot != i) // Swap rows when a better pivot was found.
920            for (std::size_t c = 0; c < N; ++c) { // Visit each matrix column.
921                T temp = a[c][i]; // Save an entry while exchanging the two rows.
922                a[c][i] = a[c][pivot]; // Update this matrix entry during row elimination or exchange.
923                a[c][pivot] = temp; // Update this matrix entry during row elimination or exchange.
924                temp = out[c][i]; // Save an entry while exchanging the two rows.
925                out[c][i] = out[c][pivot]; // Store the computed component in the independent result.
926                out[c][pivot] = temp; // Store the computed component in the independent result.
927            } // Finish this component or matrix pass.
928        T diagonal = a[i][i]; // Save the pivot value before normalizing the row.

1844/** @internal Export an embedded shader as standard GLSL, with version and declaration macros.
1845 * This function supplies the version directive. Guard the body's C++ include
1846 * with #ifdef __cplusplus. The exported source contains the selected version
1847 * and expanded declarations.
1848 */
1849inline std::string glsl_source(const std::string& source, profile p) { // Add the selected GLSL version and shared-declaration definitions.
1850    std::istringstream lines(source); // Read the embedded shader one line at a time.
1851    std::string line; // Read each embedded source line while checking version directives.
1852    while (std::getline(lines, line)) { // Inspect each source line for an unsupported version directive.
1853        std::size_t start = line.find_first_not_of(" \t\r"); // Set the beginning of the current token or range.
1854        if (start != std::string::npos && line[start] == '#') { // Choose this branch when start differs from std::string::npos and line[start] equals '#'.
1855            start = line.find_first_not_of(" \t", start + 1); // Set the beginning of the current token or range.
1856            if (start != std::string::npos && line.compare(start, 7, "version") == 0) // Choose this branch when start differs from std::string::npos and line.compare(start, 7, "version") equals 0.
1857                throw error("shared shaders must omit #version; glsl_source supplies it"); // Report shared shaders must omit #version. glsl_source supplies it.
1858        } // End this scope in glsl source.
1859    } // End this scope in glsl source.
1860    const char* version = p == profile::es31   ? "310 es" // Set the current GL version text.
1861                          : p == profile::es32 ? "320 es" // Select the version associated with this shader profile.
1862                          : p == profile::gl43 ? "430 core" // Select the version associated with this shader profile.
1863                          : p == profile::gl45 ? "450 core" // Select the version associated with this shader profile.
1864                                               : "460 core"; // Select desktop GLSL 4.60 for the remaining profile.
1865    std::string out = std::string("#version ") + version + "\n"; // Set the assembled shader text.
1866    if (p == profile::es31 || p == profile::es32) // Choose this branch when p equals profile::es31 or p equals profile::es32.
1867        out += "precision highp float;\nprecision highp int;\n"; // Set the assembled shader text.
1868    out += // Set the assembled shader text.
1869        "#define SHDR_BEGIN(name,x,y,z) layout(local_size_x=x,local_size_y=y,local_size_z=z) in;\n" // Emit a native workgroup declaration for this shader.
1870        "#define SHDR_END()\n" // Remove the host-only shader wrapper terminator.
1871        "#define SHDR_MAIN() void main()\n" // Map the shared entry-point spelling to native GLSL main.
1872        "#define SHDR_UNIFORM(t,n) uniform t n;\n" // Emit a native typed uniform declaration.
1873        "#define SHDR_SWIZZLE(v,s) (v).s\n" // Map shared swizzle syntax to native GLSL component selection.
1874        "#define SHDR_NOT(v) not(v)\n" // Map shared boolean negation to the native GLSL builtin.
1875        "#define SHDR_IN(t,n) in t n\n" // Emit a native input parameter qualifier.
1876        "#define SHDR_OUT(t,n) out t n\n" // Emit a native output parameter qualifier.
1877        "#define SHDR_INOUT(t,n) inout t n\n" // Emit a native input-output parameter qualifier.
1878        "#line 1\n"; // Restore shader line numbering before appending the original source.
1879 // Desktop GLSL accepts highp precision qualifiers from GLSL 4.10 onward.
1880    return out + detail::expand_declarations(source, p == profile::es31 || p == profile::es32); // Add the selected GLSL version and shared-declaration definitions.
1881} // End this scope in glsl source.

2100struct device_state { // Retain GL functions, context ownership, limits, and pending cleanup.
2101    gl_api gl; // Keep the retained GL function table.
2102    profile language; // Keep the selected shader profile.
2103    unsigned max_groups[3], max_local[3], max_invocations, max_buffers, max_images; // Keep work group dimensions, invocation and resource binding limits.
2104    std::shared_ptr<void> context_keepalive; // Keep the retained headless context.
2105    std::function<void()> activate_context; // Keep the callback that makes this device context current.
2106    std::thread::id context_thread; // Keep the thread allowed to issue GL commands.
2107    std::mutex retirement_mutex; // Keep the lock for deferred resource cleanup.
2108    std::vector<std::function<void(gl_api&)>> retirements; // Keep GL deletions requested by another thread.
2109    struct deferred { // Keep the deferred values and operations together.
2110        std::function<bool(gl_api&)> poll; // Keep the zero-time completion callback.
2111        std::function<void(gl_api&)> cancel; // Keep the fence-deletion callback used at shutdown.
2112    }; // End this scope in runtime.
2113    std::vector<deferred> pending_work; // Keep discarded submissions awaiting completion.
2114    bool retirements_closed; // Keep whether device teardown has stopped retaining submissions.
2115    device_state(const std::function<void*(const char*)>& resolver, profile p) // Load GL entry points and validate the selected compute profile.
2116        : gl(resolver), language(p), context_thread(std::this_thread::get_id()), // Resolve GL functions and record this context's profile and owning thread.
2117          retirements_closed(false) { // Allow pending completion leases until the public device is destroyed.
2118        const unsigned char* version = gl.GetString(VERSION); // Read the current context version before checking the requested profile.

3482 * before submitting a CPU job.

3501/** @brief Result of a completion query: completed work or an expired timeout. */
3502enum class wait_status { ready, timeout }; // Name the two outcomes of a GPU completion query.
3503
3504namespace detail { // Group these definitions in the detail namespace.
3505struct submission_resources { // Keep the submission resources values and operations together.
3506    std::vector<std::shared_ptr<resource_state>> resources; // Keep the resource storage retained until queued work completes.
3507    std::vector<std::shared_ptr<program_state>> programs; // Keep the compiled programs retained by a submission.
3508}; // End this scope in async.

3510struct submission_state { // Keep a GPU fence and its resources alive until retirement.
3511    std::shared_ptr<device_state> owner; // Keep the device that owns the GL resource.
3512    GLsync fence; // Keep the GL completion fence.
3513    std::shared_ptr<submission_resources> retained; // Keep the submission resource bundle.
3514    bool completed; // Cache whether this submission fence has already signaled.
3515    explicit submission_state(const std::shared_ptr<device_state>& d) // Retain the device, fence, and queued resource bundle.
3516        : owner(d), fence(0), retained(std::make_shared<submission_resources>()), completed(false) { // Retain the device and create an empty pending-completion resource bundle.
3517    } // End this scope in submission state.
3518    ~submission_state() noexcept { // Retire completed fences and defer pending fence cleanup.
3519        if (!fence) // Finish immediately for an empty fence.
3520            return; // Finish this operation.
3521        const GLsync sync = fence; // Copy the fence handle into the deferred cleanup callback.
3522        const std::shared_ptr<submission_resources> keep = retained; // Retain buffers and programs until deferred cleanup releases this bundle.
3523        try { // Keep cleanup available if an allocation, shader, or driver operation fails.
3524            if (completed) { // Retire a fence whose completion has already been observed.
3525                owner->retire([sync, keep](gl_api& gl) { // Delete on the context thread or defer deletion to that thread.
3526                    gl.DeleteSync(sync); // Delete the GL completion fence.
3527                    (void)keep; // Keep the resource references captured for this cleanup.
3528                }); // End this scope in submission state.
3529            } else { // Handle the alternative resource or completion case.
3530 // The context thread checks this retirement entry with a zero timeout.
3531                owner->defer_poll( // Retain a completion check until its fence signals.
3532                    [sync, keep](gl_api& gl) -> bool { // Retain these captures until the queued callback finishes.
3533                        const GLenum status = gl.ClientWaitSync(sync, 0, 0); // Poll the discarded fence with zero flags and a zero timeout.
3534                        if (status == TIMEOUT_EXPIRED) // Check the driver result before marking GPU completion.
3535                            return false; // Keep the discarded submission pending while its fence is unsignaled.
3536                        gl.DeleteSync(sync); // Delete the GL completion fence.
3537                        (void)keep; // Keep the resource references captured for this cleanup.
3538                        return true; // Remove the retired fence and release its retained resource bundle.
3539                    }, // End this scope in submission state.
3540                    [sync](gl_api& gl) { // Keep only the fence handle for nonblocking shutdown cancellation.
3541                        gl.DeleteSync(sync); // Delete the GL completion fence.
3542                    }); // End this scope in submission state.
3543            } // End this scope in submission state.
3544        } catch (...) { // Preserve cleanup or exception propagation for this failed operation.
3545 // Destruction defers pending fence cleanup. GL command references keep
3546 // already queued operations valid if allocating a retirement entry fails.
3547        } // End this scope in submission state.
3548    } // End this scope in submission state.
3549    wait_status query(GLuint64 timeout) { // Check completion with the requested driver timeout.
3550        owner->require_thread(); // Require the device context thread and activate its headless context.
3551        if (completed) // Reuse the cached completion result after checking the context thread.
3552            return wait_status::ready; // Tell the caller that queued GPU commands have completed.
3553        const GLenum result = owner->gl.ClientWaitSync(fence, 0, timeout); // Check a GPU fence with the caller-selected timeout.
3554        if (result == ALREADY_SIGNALED || result == CONDITION_SATISFIED) { // Check the driver result before marking GPU completion.
3555            completed = true; // Set whether the GPU fence has already signaled.
3556            return wait_status::ready; // Tell the caller that queued GPU commands have completed.
3557        } // End this scope in query.
3558        if (result == TIMEOUT_EXPIRED) // Check the driver result before marking GPU completion.
3559            return wait_status::timeout; // Tell the caller that the explicit wait expired before completion.
3560        owner->gl.check("query GPU submission"); // Check for a driver error from the preceding GL operation.
3561        throw error("GPU completion query failed"); // Report gpu completion query failed.
3562    } // End this scope in query.
3563}; // End this scope in async.
3564} // namespace detail

3566/** @brief A movable handle for one queued GPU pipeline.

3568 * driver wait. wait() explicitly waits for completion. Destroying a handle

3576        : state_(std::move(state)) { // Move the fence state into this completion handle.
3577    } // End this scope in async.

3586    submission(const submission&) = delete; // Prevent copying this object and duplicating its retained identity.
3587    submission& operator=(const submission&) = delete; // Prevent copying this object and duplicating its retained identity.
3588    /** @brief Return whether this handle represents submitted GPU commands. */

3591    } // End this scope in async.

3595    } // End this scope in ready.
3596    /** @brief Request a driver wait with a nonnegative timeout in nanoseconds. */
3597    wait_status wait(std::chrono::nanoseconds timeout) { // Apply the explicit completion wait selected by the caller.
3598        if (timeout.count() < 0) // Require a nonnegative wait duration.
3599            throw error("GPU submission timeout must be nonnegative"); // Report gpu submission timeout must be nonnegative.
3600        if (!state_) // Treat an empty handle as already completed.
3601            return wait_status::ready; // Tell the caller that queued GPU commands have completed.
3602        return state_->query(static_cast<detail::GLuint64>(timeout.count())); // Apply the explicit completion wait selected by the caller.
3603    } // End this scope in wait.
3604    /** @brief Explicitly wait until submitted commands complete. */
3605    wait_status wait() { // Apply the explicit completion wait selected by the caller.
3606        if (!state_) // Treat an empty handle as already completed.
3607            return wait_status::ready; // Tell the caller that queued GPU commands have completed.
3608        while (state_->query((std::numeric_limits<detail::GLuint64>::max)()) == // Use the caller's explicit blocking wait until the fence completes.
3609               wait_status::timeout) { // Repeat only if the implementation still reports an incomplete wait.
3610        } // End this scope in wait.
3611        return wait_status::ready; // Tell the caller that queued GPU commands have completed.
3612    } // End this scope in wait.
3613}; // End this scope in async.

3615/** @brief Enqueue all GPU stages and return a fence for polling or explicit waits.
3616 * Each stage must support GPU execution. Call prepare()
3617 * before entering a latency-sensitive loop to compile shaders and allocate/upload
3618 * resources in advance. Subsequent host edits can still require an upload.
3619 * Uniform and binding changes after return affect subsequent submissions.
3620 */
3621inline submission pipeline::submit(device& d) const { // Queue compute work and return its completion handle.
3622    d.state()->require_thread(); // Require the device context thread and activate its headless context.
3623    const std::vector<stage>& commands = stages(); // Read the ordered stages that this submission will queue.
3624    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < commands.size(); ++i) // Visit each ordered GPU stage in this submission.
3625        if (commands[i].target == backend::cpu) // Reject explicit CPU stages before queueing any GPU commands.
3626            throw error("GPU submission cannot contain CPU stages"); // Require GPU stages for GPU submission.
3627    if (commands.empty()) // Skip fence creation for an empty pipeline.
3628        return submission(); // Represent an empty pipeline with an already completed handle.
3629    std::unique_ptr<detail::submission_state> completion(new detail::submission_state(d.state())); // Retain the device, fence, and queued resource bundle.
3630    completion->retained->programs.reserve(commands.size()); // Reserve room to retain one compiled program per stage.
3631    prepare(d); // Compile the program and prepare its bound GPU resources.
3632    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < commands.size(); ++i) { // Visit each ordered GPU stage in this submission.
3633        const std::vector<std::shared_ptr<detail::resource_state>> resources = // Set the resource storage retained until queued work completes.
3634            commands[i].shader->resources(); // Collect the shared storage used by this shader.
3635        completion->retained->resources.insert( // Retain this entry in the ordered resource or work collection.
3636            completion->retained->resources.end(), resources.begin(), resources.end()); // Keep the end of the current range.
3637        completion->retained->programs.push_back(commands[i].shader->program_state()); // Retain this entry in the ordered resource or work collection.
3638    } // End this scope in submit.
3639    try { // Keep cleanup available if an allocation, shader, or driver operation fails.
3640        run(d); // Queue all validated GPU stages in pipeline order.
3641    } catch (...) { // Preserve cleanup or exception propagation for this failed operation.
3642 // A later dispatch can fail after an earlier dispatch was queued.
3643        completion->fence = d.state()->gl.FenceSync(detail::SYNC_GPU_COMMANDS_COMPLETE, 0); // Insert a completion fence after queued compute work.
3644        d.state()->gl.Flush(); // Flush queued GPU commands for driver execution.
3645        throw; // Rethrow the original failure after arranging the necessary cleanup.
3646    } // End this scope in submit.
3647    completion->fence = d.state()->gl.FenceSync(detail::SYNC_GPU_COMMANDS_COMPLETE, 0); // Insert a completion fence after queued compute work.
3648    if (!completion->fence) { // Check that the driver allocated a valid completion fence.
3649        d.state()->gl.check("create GPU submission fence"); // Expose retained runtime state to the resource and backend helpers.
3650        throw error("cannot create GPU submission fence"); // Report completion-fence allocation failure.
3651    } // End this scope in submit.
3652    d.state()->gl.Flush(); // Flush queued GPU commands for driver execution.
3653    d.state()->gl.check("submit GPU pipeline"); // Expose retained runtime state to the resource and backend helpers.
3654    return submission(std::move(completion)); // Queue compute work and return its completion handle.
3655} // End this scope in submit.

3657/** @brief A bounded CPU executor for independent pipeline jobs.
3658 * Each submit() snapshots kernels, uniforms and resource bindings. Snapshots
3659 * have independent invocation state, while buffers and images retain shared
3660 * storage. Give concurrent jobs distinct writable resources, such as ring slots.
3661 * Queue saturation throws immediately. Futures report results or exceptions.
3662 * Destroying a future releases its result handle, while the executor retains
3663 * the job until completion. shutdown() drains accepted jobs and joins workers.
3664 * Executor destruction also drains and joins them.

3666class executor { // Keep the executor values and operations together.
3667    struct job { // Keep the job values and operations together.
3668        std::function<void()> function; // Keep the application function executed by a CPU worker.
3669        std::promise<void> completion; // Keep the completion result that the caller will receive.
3670        explicit job(const std::function<void()>& fn) : function(fn) { // Keep the accepted CPU function and its promise result.
3671        } // End this scope in async.
3672    }; // End this scope in async.
3673    struct queue_state { // Share the bounded queue between its producer and workers.
3674        std::mutex mutex; // Keep the lock protecting shared state.
3675        std::condition_variable changed; // Wake sleeping workers when work or shutdown state changes.
3676        std::deque<std::shared_ptr<job>> jobs; // Keep accepted CPU work awaiting an available worker.
3677        std::vector<std::thread::id> worker_ids; // Keep the worker thread identifiers used to reject self-joining.
3678        std::size_t pending, capacity; // Keep the current pending count and the maximum queue size.
3679        bool closing; // Keep whether the CPU executor is draining for shutdown.
3680        explicit queue_state(std::size_t n) : pending(0), capacity(n), closing(false) { // Start an empty queue with the chosen pending-job capacity.
3681        } // End this scope in async.
3682    }; // End this scope in async.
3683    std::shared_ptr<queue_state> state_; // Share the bounded queue between the executor and its workers.
3684    std::vector<std::thread> workers_; // Keep the threads that execute accepted CPU jobs.
3685    std::mutex shutdown_mutex_; // Keep the lock that serializes executor shutdown.
3686
3687    static void consume(const std::shared_ptr<queue_state>& state) { // Take accepted jobs from the queue and execute them on this worker.
3688        for (;;) { // Keep this worker available until its queue is drained for shutdown.
3689            std::shared_ptr<job> next; // Keep the CPU job selected by this worker.
3690            { // Begin the protected scope for this operation.
3691                std::unique_lock<std::mutex> lock(state->mutex); // Hold the mutex while this shared state is accessed.
3692                state->changed.wait(lock, [&] { // Release the queue lock while sleeping until work or shutdown arrives.
3693                    return state->closing || !state->jobs.empty(); // Wake the worker for a queued job or an explicit shutdown.
3694                }); // End this scope in consume.
3695                if (state->jobs.empty()) // Exit only when shutdown has awakened an empty queue.
3696                    return; // Finish this operation.
3697                next = state->jobs.front(); // Set the CPU job selected by this worker.
3698                state->jobs.pop_front(); // Remove this accepted job from the pending queue.
3699                --state->pending; // Release its pending slot before executing the job.
3700            } // End this scope in consume.
3701            try { // Keep cleanup available if an allocation, shader, or driver operation fails.
3702                next->function(); // Execute the selected application function or CPU pipeline snapshot.
3703                next->function = std::function<void()>(); // Release kernel and resource captures before publishing completion.
3704                next->completion.set_value(); // Publish successful completion after the job releases its captures.
3705            } catch (...) { // Preserve cleanup or exception propagation for this failed operation.
3706                const std::exception_ptr failure = std::current_exception(); // Set the exception captured from a CPU job.
3707                next->function = std::function<void()>(); // Release kernel and resource captures before publishing completion.
3708                next->completion.set_exception(failure); // Deliver the worker failure through the caller completion future.
3709            } // End this scope in consume.
3710        } // End this scope in consume.
3711    } // End this scope in consume.
3712    void reserve() { // Reserve capacity and report a full queue immediately.
3713        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(state_->mutex); // Hold the mutex while this shared state is accessed.
3714        if (state_->closing) // Check the queue state before accepting or executing work.
3715            throw error("CPU executor is shut down"); // Report cpu executor is shut down.
3716        if (state_->pending == state_->capacity) // Check the queue state before accepting or executing work.
3717            throw error("CPU executor queue is full"); // Report cpu executor queue is full.
3718        ++state_->pending; // Count the accepted job against the pending queue capacity.

3720    void abandon() noexcept { // Release the reserved slot after a submission failure.
3721        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(state_->mutex); // Hold the mutex while this shared state is accessed.
3722        --state_->pending; // Return the queue slot reserved by an unsuccessful submission.
3723    } // End this scope in abandon.
3724    std::future<void> append_reserved(const std::function<void()>& function) { // Attach the accepted CPU job to its reserved queue slot.
3725        std::shared_ptr<job> work(new job(function)); // Keep the application function executed by a CPU worker.
3726        std::future<void> result = work->completion.get_future(); // Set the value returned by this operation.
3727        { // Begin the protected scope for this operation.
3728            std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(state_->mutex); // Hold the mutex while this shared state is accessed.
3729            if (state_->closing) // Check the queue state before accepting or executing work.
3730                throw error("CPU executor is shut down"); // Report cpu executor is shut down.

3737  public: // Expose the operations callers can use.
3738    /** @brief Start workers with room for at most capacity pending jobs.
3739     * Capacity counts jobs waiting for a worker. Both arguments must be positive.
3740     */
3741    explicit executor(std::size_t workers = 1, std::size_t capacity = 64) // Start a fixed number of workers with a bounded pending-job queue.
3742        : state_(std::make_shared<queue_state>(capacity)) { // Keep the maximum number of pending CPU jobs.
3743        if (!workers || !capacity) // Require positive worker and queue counts.
3744            throw error("CPU executor requires positive worker and queue counts"); // Report cpu executor requires positive worker and queue counts.

3746        state_->worker_ids.reserve(workers); // Allocate space for every worker thread identifier.
3747        try { // Keep cleanup available if an allocation, shader, or driver operation fails.
3748            for (std::size_t i = 0; i < workers; ++i) { // Visit this axis of the dispatch or current workgroup.
3749                const std::shared_ptr<queue_state> state = state_; // Set the shared device or worker state.
3750                workers_.push_back(std::thread([state] { // Retain this entry in the ordered resource or work collection.
3751                    consume(state); // Take accepted jobs from the queue and execute them on this worker.
3752                })); // End this scope in executor.
3753                state_->worker_ids.push_back(workers_.back().get_id()); // Retain this entry in the ordered resource or work collection.
3754            } // End this scope in executor.

3756            shutdown(); // Drain accepted CPU work and join the workers from an application thread.

3759    } // End this scope in executor.
3760    ~executor() { // Drain accepted work and join the CPU workers at explicit pool teardown.
3761        shutdown(); // Drain accepted CPU work and join the workers from an application thread.

3763    executor(const executor&) = delete; // Prevent copying this object and duplicating its retained identity.
3764    executor& operator=(const executor&) = delete; // Prevent copying this object and duplicating its retained identity.
3765    /** @brief Snapshot a host-ready CPU pipeline, enqueue it and return a future.
3766     * Each stage must support CPU execution and have current host data.
3767     */
3768    std::future<void> submit(const pipeline& source) { // Queue compute work and return its completion handle.
3769        reserve(); // Reserve capacity and report a full queue immediately.
3770        try { // Keep cleanup available if an allocation, shader, or driver operation fails.
3771            source.require_host_ready(); // Validate CPU stages and host-ready resources before queueing.
3772            const pipeline copy = source.snapshot(); // Capture isolated kernel interfaces and the current bindings and uniforms.

3774                copy.run(); // Execute the retained CPU snapshot on its worker thread.

3776        } catch (...) { // Preserve cleanup or exception propagation for this failed operation.
3777            abandon(); // Release the reserved slot after a submission failure.

3781    /** @brief Enqueue an application CPU function on the same bounded queue.

3786        try { // Keep cleanup available if an allocation, shader, or driver operation fails.
3787            return append_reserved(std::function<void()>(function)); // Queue the application callback on the bounded CPU executor.
3788        } catch (...) { // Preserve cleanup or exception propagation for this failed operation.
3789            abandon(); // Release the reserved slot after a submission failure.
3790            throw; // Rethrow the original failure after arranging the necessary cleanup.
3791        } // End this scope in enqueue.
3792    } // End this scope in enqueue.
3793    /** @brief Return the count of queued or currently being constructed jobs. */

3797    } // End this scope in pending.
3798    /** @brief Return the maximum number of pending jobs. */

3800        return state_->capacity; // Return the configured pending-job limit.
3801    } // End this scope in capacity.
3802    /** @brief Return the number of worker threads. */

3804        return workers_.size(); // Return the number of worker threads.
3805    } // End this scope in workers.
3806    /** @brief Drain accepted jobs and join all workers. later submissions fail.

3809    void shutdown() { // Drain accepted CPU work and join the workers from an application thread.

3811                      state_->worker_ids.end(), // Keep the end of the current range.
3812                      std::this_thread::get_id()) != state_->worker_ids.end()) // Reject joining the current executor worker from its own job.
3813            throw error("CPU executor shutdown requires an application thread"); // Report cpu executor shutdown requires an application thread.

3815        { // Begin the protected scope for this operation.
3816            std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(state_->mutex); // Hold the mutex while this shared state is accessed.
3817            state_->closing = true; // Set whether the CPU executor is draining for shutdown.
3818        } // End this scope in shutdown.
3819        state_->changed.notify_all(); // Wake workers so they can observe new queue or shutdown state.
3820        for (std::size_t i = 0; i < workers_.size(); ++i) // Visit each CPU worker during lifecycle handling.
3821            if (workers_[i].joinable()) // Choose this branch when workers [i].joinable().
3822                workers_[i].join(); // Join this CPU worker after accepted work has drained.
3823    } // End this scope in shutdown.
3824}; // End this scope in async.

3852inline backend_unavailable egl_failure(const char* operation) { // Build a readable diagnostic from the EGL error code.

3854    std::ostringstream message; // Build a readable diagnostic from the EGL error code.

3856    return backend_unavailable(message.str()); // Build a readable diagnostic from the EGL error code.
3857} // End this scope in egl failure.

3859 // Initialization and the last termination share a lock, including during weak-pointer expiry.
3860struct egl_display_registry { // Keep the egl display registry values and operations together.
3861    std::mutex mutex; // Keep the lock protecting shared state.
3862    EGLDisplay display; // Keep the initialized EGL display.
3863    std::size_t owners; // Keep the number of contexts retaining this display.
3864    egl_display_registry() : display(EGL_NO_DISPLAY), owners(0) { // Start the initialized-display owner count at zero.
3865    } // End this scope in egl.
3866}; // End this scope in egl.
3867inline egl_display_registry& egl_displays() { // Share the display-lifetime registry among headless devices.
3868    static egl_display_registry registry; // Keep the shared display lifetime registry.
3869    return registry; // Return the shared display lifetime registry.
3870} // End this scope in egl displays.

3872 // Contexts share one initialized display. the last context releases it.
3873struct egl_display_state { // Keep the egl display state values and operations together.
3874    EGLDisplay display; // Keep the initialized EGL display.
3875    egl_display_state() : display(EGL_NO_DISPLAY) { // Retain one initialized EGL display for living contexts.
3876        egl_display_registry& registry = egl_displays(); // Set the shared display lifetime registry.
3877        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(registry.mutex); // Hold the mutex while this shared state is accessed.
3878        if (registry.owners) { // Reuse this display when another context already retains its initialization.
3879            display = registry.display; // Set the initialized EGL display.
3880            ++registry.owners; // Retain the existing initialized display for this new owner.
3881            return; // Finish this operation.
3882        } // End this scope in egl display state.
3883        typedef EGLDisplay(EGLAPIENTRYP platform_display_fn)(EGLenum, void*, const EGLint*); // Name the representation used by this GL or shader interface.
3884        const platform_display_fn platform_display = // Resolve the optional surfaceless display entry point.
3885            reinterpret_cast<platform_display_fn>(eglGetProcAddress("eglGetPlatformDisplayEXT")); // Look up the requested GL entry point through EGL.
3886        if (platform_display) { // Choose this branch when platform display.
3887 // Mesa's surfaceless platform creates an offscreen display on supported drivers.
3888            display = platform_display(0x31DD, EGL_DEFAULT_DISPLAY, 0); // Set the initialized EGL display.
3889            if (display != EGL_NO_DISPLAY && !eglInitialize(display, 0, 0)) // Prepare the default-display fallback if surfaceless initialization fails.
3890                display = EGL_NO_DISPLAY; // Set the initialized EGL display.
3891        } // End this scope in egl display state.
3892        if (display == EGL_NO_DISPLAY) { // Try the default display after the surfaceless path.
3893            display = eglGetDisplay(EGL_DEFAULT_DISPLAY); // Set the initialized EGL display.
3894            if (display == EGL_NO_DISPLAY || !eglInitialize(display, 0, 0)) { // Report failure to acquire and initialize the default display.
3895                display = EGL_NO_DISPLAY; // Set the initialized EGL display.
3896                throw egl_failure("EGL display"); // Report egl display.
3897            } // End this scope in egl display state.
3898        } // End this scope in egl display state.
3899        registry.display = display; // Set the initialized EGL display.
3900        registry.owners = 1; // Set the number of contexts retaining this display.
3901    } // End this scope in egl display state.
3902    ~egl_display_state() { // Release this object's owned resources at teardown.
3903        egl_display_registry& registry = egl_displays(); // Set the shared display lifetime registry.
3904        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(registry.mutex); // Hold the mutex while this shared state is accessed.
3905        if (display != EGL_NO_DISPLAY && --registry.owners == 0) { // Terminate an initialized display after its final context owner releases it.
3906            eglTerminate(display); // Terminate the display after its last context owner is released.
3907            registry.display = EGL_NO_DISPLAY; // Set the initialized EGL display.
3908        } // End this scope in egl display state.
3909    } // End this scope in egl display state.
3910    egl_display_state(const egl_display_state&) = delete; // Prevent copying this object and duplicating its retained identity.
3911    egl_display_state& operator=(const egl_display_state&) = delete; // Prevent copying this object and duplicating its retained identity.
3912}; // End this scope in egl.

3914inline std::shared_ptr<egl_display_state> acquire_egl_display() { // Reuse the initialized display while any context retains it.
3915    static std::mutex mutex; // Keep the lock protecting shared state.
3916    static std::weak_ptr<egl_display_state> cached; // Keep the weak reference to the shared EGL display.
3917    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(mutex); // Hold the mutex while this shared state is accessed.
3918    std::shared_ptr<egl_display_state> display = cached.lock(); // Set the initialized EGL display.
3919    if (!display) { // Create the shared display state for its first owner.
3920        display = std::make_shared<egl_display_state>(); // Set the initialized EGL display.
3921        cached = display; // Set the weak reference to the shared EGL display.
3922    } // End this scope in acquire egl display.
3923    return display; // Return the initialized EGL display.
3924} // End this scope in acquire egl display.

3926struct egl_context_state { // Retain one headless EGL display, context, and pbuffer.
3927    std::shared_ptr<egl_display_state> display; // Keep the initialized EGL display.
3928    EGLContext context; // Keep the EGL context used for compute commands.
3929    EGLSurface surface; // Keep the one-pixel EGL pbuffer.
3930    EGLenum api; // Keep the selected desktop GL or GLES API.
3931    std::thread::id thread; // Keep the thread that created this EGL context.
3932
3933    explicit egl_context_state(profile p) // Create a pbuffer context for the requested shader profile.
3934        : display(acquire_egl_display()), context(EGL_NO_CONTEXT), surface(EGL_NO_SURFACE), // Reuse the initialized display while any context retains it.
3935          api(p == profile::es31 || p == profile::es32 ? EGL_OPENGL_ES_API : EGL_OPENGL_API), // Choose the EGL client API matching the requested shader profile.
3936          thread(std::this_thread::get_id()) { // Remember the only thread allowed to use this EGL context.
3937        try { // Keep cleanup available if an allocation, shader, or driver operation fails.
3938            const bool desktop = p != profile::es31 && p != profile::es32; // Select the API family for the requested profile.
3939            if (!eglBindAPI(api)) // Check that EGL accepts the selected graphics API.
3940                throw egl_failure("EGL graphics API"); // Report egl graphics api.
3941            const EGLint config_attributes[] = {EGL_SURFACE_TYPE, // Request a pbuffer configuration with the chosen client API.
3942                                                EGL_PBUFFER_BIT, // Request a configuration capable of creating a small offscreen surface.
3943                                                EGL_RENDERABLE_TYPE, // Select the client API supported by the framebuffer configuration.
3944                                                desktop ? EGL_OPENGL_BIT : 0x0040, // Request desktop GL or an OpenGL ES 3-capable configuration.
3945                                                EGL_RED_SIZE, // Specify the number of red bits in the offscreen surface.
3946                                                8, // Request eight bits for this color component.
3947                                                EGL_GREEN_SIZE, // Specify the number of green bits in the offscreen surface.
3948                                                8, // Request eight bits for this color component.
3949                                                EGL_BLUE_SIZE, // Specify the number of blue bits in the offscreen surface.
3950                                                8, // Request eight bits for this color component.
3951                                                EGL_NONE}; // Create a pbuffer context for the requested shader profile.
3952            EGLConfig config = 0; // Set the selected EGL framebuffer configuration.
3953            EGLint count = 0; // Set the element or configuration count.
3954            if (!eglChooseConfig(display->display, config_attributes, &config, 1, &count) || !count) // Check resource size or driver limits before accessing storage.
3955                throw egl_failure("EGL framebuffer configuration"); // Report egl framebuffer configuration.
3956            const EGLint major = desktop ? 4 : 3; // Set the GL major version.
3957            const EGLint minor = p == profile::es31   ? 1 // Set the GL minor version.
3958                                 : p == profile::es32 ? 2 // Select the version associated with this shader profile.
3959                                 : p == profile::gl43 ? 3 // Select the version associated with this shader profile.
3960                                 : p == profile::gl45 ? 5 // Select the version associated with this shader profile.
3961                                                      : 6; // Select minor version six for the desktop GL 4.6 profile.
3962 // These KHR_create_context attributes are also core in EGL 1.5.
3963            const EGLint desktop_attributes[] = { // Request the selected desktop version and core profile.
3964                0x3098, major, 0x30FB, minor, 0x30FD, 0x00000001, EGL_NONE}; // Create a pbuffer context for the requested shader profile.
3965            const EGLint es_attributes[] = {0x3098, major, 0x30FB, minor, EGL_NONE}; // Request the selected GLES major and minor versions.
3966            context = eglCreateContext(display->display, // Create a compute context for the requested GL or GLES version.
3967                                       config, // Keep the selected EGL framebuffer configuration.
3968                                       EGL_NO_CONTEXT, // Create a context with its own GL object namespace.
3969                                       desktop ? desktop_attributes : es_attributes); // Create a pbuffer context for the requested shader profile.
3970            if (context == EGL_NO_CONTEXT) // Check that the driver created the requested context.
3971                throw egl_failure("Requested GL context"); // Report requested gl context.
3972            const EGLint surface_attributes[] = {EGL_WIDTH, 1, EGL_HEIGHT, 1, EGL_NONE}; // Create a one-pixel offscreen pbuffer for compute commands.
3973            surface = eglCreatePbufferSurface(display->display, config, surface_attributes); // Set the one-pixel EGL pbuffer.
3974            if (surface == EGL_NO_SURFACE) // Check that the driver created the offscreen pbuffer.
3975                throw egl_failure("EGL pbuffer"); // Report egl pbuffer.
3976            make_current(); // Select this context on its creating thread.
3977        } catch (...) { // Preserve cleanup or exception propagation for this failed operation.
3978            release(); // Release this surface and context while preserving other active contexts.
3979            throw; // Rethrow the original failure after arranging the necessary cleanup.
3980        } // End this scope in egl context state.
3981    } // End this scope in egl context state.
3982    void make_current() const { // Select this context on its creating thread.
3983        if (std::this_thread::get_id() != thread) // Check that the operation uses the context or lifecycle thread.
3984            throw error("headless EGL operations require the context's creating thread"); // Report headless egl operations require the context's creating thread.
3985        if (!eglBindAPI(api)) // Check that EGL accepts the selected graphics API.
3986            throw egl_failure("EGL graphics API"); // Report egl graphics api.
3987        if (eglGetCurrentContext() == context && eglGetCurrentDisplay() == display->display) // Choose this branch when eglGetCurrentContext() equals context and eglGetCurrentDisplay() equals display->display.

3991    } // End this scope in make current.
3992    void release() { // Release this surface and context while preserving other active contexts.
3993 // Unbind this context only when it is current on this thread.

3996        if (context != EGL_NO_CONTEXT && eglGetCurrentContext() == context) // Unbind this context when it is current.
3997            eglMakeCurrent(display->display, EGL_NO_SURFACE, EGL_NO_SURFACE, EGL_NO_CONTEXT); // Make this pbuffer context current on its owning thread.
3998        if (surface != EGL_NO_SURFACE) // Destroy the pbuffer allocated by this state.

4001            eglDestroyContext(display->display, context); // Release the EGL object after its context-thread owners finish.
4002        if (previous_api != api) // Choose this branch when previous api differs from api.
4003            eglBindAPI(previous_api); // Restore the API binding that belonged to the other live context.
4004        surface = EGL_NO_SURFACE; // Set the one-pixel EGL pbuffer.
4005        context = EGL_NO_CONTEXT; // Set the EGL context used for compute commands.
4006    } // End this scope in release.
4007    ~egl_context_state() { // Release this object's owned resources at teardown.
4008        release(); // Release this surface and context while preserving other active contexts.
4009    } // End this scope in egl context state.
4010    egl_context_state(const egl_context_state&) = delete; // Prevent copying this object and duplicating its retained identity.
4011    egl_context_state& operator=(const egl_context_state&) = delete; // Prevent copying this object and duplicating its retained identity.
4012}; // End this scope in egl.

4019/** @brief An optional, headless EGL pbuffer context for a selected compute profile.
4020 * Define SHDR_ENABLE_EGL=1 before including shdr.h and link EGL to use this class.
4021 * It prefers a surfaceless display and otherwise uses EGL's default display.
4022 * Create, use and finally release the context on its creating thread. Displays
4023 * are shared among living shdr contexts. Let shdr manage their display lifetime.
4024 */
4025class headless_context { // Keep the headless context values and operations together.
4026    std::shared_ptr<detail::egl_context_state> context_; // Keep the retained headless context state.
4027
4028  public: // Expose the operations callers can use.
4029    /** @brief Create a 1-by-1 pbuffer and make its context current.
4030     * @param p Minimum GL or GLES version. defaults to OpenGL ES 3.1.
4031     * @throws backend_unavailable If backend initialization fails.
4032     */
4033    explicit headless_context(profile p = profile::es31) : context_(detail::make_egl_context(p)) { // Create and retain an EGL context for the requested compute profile.
4034    } // End this scope in egl.
4035    /** @brief Make this context current on its creating thread. */
4036    void make_current() const { // Select this context on its creating thread.
4037        context_->make_current(); // Select this context on its creating thread.
4038    } // End this scope in make current.
4039    /** @brief Resolve a GL entry point through EGL, for shdr::device or external GL calls. */
4040    static void* resolve(const char* name) { // Resolve a named GL function through EGL.
4041        const __eglMustCastToProperFunctionPointerType function = eglGetProcAddress(name); // Look up the requested GL entry point through EGL.
4042        static_assert(sizeof(function) == sizeof(void*), // Require a representation that matches the shader interface.
4043                      "EGL function addresses must fit in void*"); // Require EGL function addresses to fit the portable resolver representation.
4044        void* address = 0; // Set the resolved GL function address.
4045        std::memcpy(&address, &function, sizeof(address)); // Copy the representation with the alias-safe byte-copy operation.
4046        return address; // Return the resolved GL function address.
4047    } // End this scope in resolve.
4048    headless_context(const headless_context&) = delete; // Prevent copying this object and duplicating its retained identity.
4049    headless_context& operator=(const headless_context&) = delete; // Prevent copying this object and duplicating its retained identity.
4050}; // End this scope in egl.

4052/** @brief A compute device that creates and retains its own headless EGL context.
4053 * Define SHDR_ENABLE_EGL=1 and link EGL. Construct this device on the thread that
4054 * performs its GPU operations. Its context remains alive while GPU resources,
4055 * programs and submissions retain the device state. release those objects on
4056 * that thread before shutdown. CPU execution uses host resources.
4057 */
4058class headless_device : public device { // Keep the headless device values and operations together.
4059    std::shared_ptr<detail::egl_context_state> context_; // Keep the retained headless context state.
4060    headless_device(const std::shared_ptr<detail::egl_context_state>& context, profile p) try // Connect the retained EGL context to the GL runtime.
4061        : device(headless_context::resolve, p), context_(context) { // Retain a validated GL device state.
4062        state()->context_keepalive = context; // Set the retained headless context.
4063        state()->activate_context = [context] { // Set the callback that makes this device context current.
4064            context->make_current(); // Select this context on its creating thread.
4065        }; // End this scope in state.

4072  public: // Expose the operations callers can use.

4077    explicit headless_device(profile p = profile::es31) // Create a compute device with its own retained EGL context.
4078        : headless_device(detail::make_egl_context(p), p) { // Connect the retained EGL context to the GL runtime.
4079    } // End this scope in headless device.

4081    void make_current() const { // Select this context on its creating thread.

4083    } // End this scope in make current.
4084    headless_device(const headless_device&) = delete; // Prevent copying this object and duplicating its retained identity.
4085    headless_device& operator=(const headless_device&) = delete; // Prevent copying this object and duplicating its retained identity.
4086}; // End this scope in egl.

4096/** @brief Begin one shared shader declaration with a fixed local work group size. */
4097#define SHDR_BEGIN(name, x, y, z) /* Start the shared shader type and its CPU snapshot method. */ \
4098    using namespace ::shdr::glsl; /* Make the GLSL math names available inside this shader. */ \
4099    struct name : ::shdr::kernel { /* Give the shared shader the CPU kernel interface. */ \
4100        name() : ::shdr::kernel(#name, ::shdr::extent(x, y, z)) { /* Store the shader name and fixed local work group size. */ \
4101        } /* Close the generated method or shader declaration. */ \
4102        std::unique_ptr<::shdr::kernel> clone() const override { /* Build an independent CPU instance for deferred execution. */ \
4103            std::unique_ptr<name> copy(new name); /* Allocate the shader instance that will hold the snapshot. */ \
4104            copy_interfaces(*copy); /* Copy uniform values and resource bindings into that instance. */ \
4105            return std::unique_ptr<::shdr::kernel>(copy.release()); /* Return ownership through the common kernel interface. */ \
4106        } /* Close the generated method or shader declaration. */
4107/** @brief End a shared shader declaration. */
4108#define SHDR_END() /* Close the shared shader type. */ \
4109    } /* Close the generated method or shader declaration. */ \
4110    ; /* Finish the generated shader type declaration. */

4138#define SHDR_SWIZZLE(value, pattern) (value).template swizzle<SHDR_DETAIL_SWIZZLE_##pattern>() // Translate component letters into a safe CPU component selection.
